newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokai Bank says may not recover loans to All Corp.
newsitem.headline: Tokai Bank says may not recover loans to All Corp.

text.p: Tokai Bank Ltd said on Monday it may not be able to recover loans extended to troubled All Corp but added that this would have no big impact on the bank's earnings for the year to March 31, 1997.
Tokai's outstanding loans to All Corp, a Tokyo-based non-bank financial institution, amounted to 56.33 billion yen as of March 23, the bank said in a statement.
As most of the loans were already covered by reserves in 1995/96, the bank's present earnings forecast for 1996/97 is unlikely to be dented much, the bank said.
Tokai Bank is the largest shareholder of All Corp, owning a 25.75 percent stake in the company.
Last week, All Corp sought court-protected special liquidation at Tokyo District Court with total debts of 350 billion yen.

In the aftermath of the bursting of the late 1980s "bubble" of inflated asset prices, All Corp was burdened with soured non-performing loans and the situation worsened due to sluggish real estate markets and bankruptcies of some of its borrowers.
Trade in All Corp shares has already been halted on the over-the-counter market.
